- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect bearish sentiment reversal.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive; apply lagged correction: subtract 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude from forecast 3–5 days later.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in high-sentiment environments (e.g., sentiment >0.67 for 5+ days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply “sentiment pivot” rule: increase forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
